context.why: US-1 built Document and Version. A version currently has no lifecycle at all: it exists, it holds Markdown, and nothing distinguishes one that has been put in front of people from one that is still being written. This story adds that lifecycle and the single act that drives it. A version starts as a draft with no standing, publishing makes it the one in force, and whatever was in force before it becomes superseded. Publishing only goes one way — there is no route back to draft and no route that makes a superseded version current again, and the absence is asserted by name so a later convenience cannot be added quietly. Immutability of a published version's wording is the NEXT story; do not build it here.

prior_decisions: D3 — publication takes effect immediately. There is no scheduled or future-dated publish, and no field holding an effective date. The version in force is stored, never computed from a clock.

D4 — no rollback. Restoring earlier wording means publishing that wording again as a new version. Build no `unpublish`, `revert`, `rollback`, `restore` or `make_current`, on the model or on any queryset.

D9 — refusals raise this package's own exceptions, never `ValidationError`. `ValidationError` is what form and admin code catches broadly, and swallowing an invariant breach into a field error is the silent discard FR-012 forbids.

D11 — the partial unique constraint and the row lock are BOTH load-bearing and which one carries depends on the backend. MySQL and MariaDB do not support partial indexes and Django omits the constraint there rather than failing (models.W036), so on those backends the `select_for_update()` lock is the only thing holding FR-007. Ship both, and put a comment at the lock saying why it is not belt-and-braces.

acceptance.given_when_then: Given a newly created version, when it is inspected, then it is a draft, it is not the version in force, and it has no publication time; when its Markdown is changed and saved, then the change is kept; and when it is deleted, then it is gone.

Given a document with no published version, when its first draft is published, then that version is in force and the document has no superseded versions; given a document with a version in force, when a second version is published, then the second is in force and the first is superseded, and exactly one version answers as in force; given an already-published version, when publishing is attempted again, then it is refused with PublishError and nothing about the document changes.

Given the Version model, when a version is created, then its status is the draft value and its published_at is null; and when a row is forced into a state where the two disagree — a draft carrying a publication time, or a published version without one — then the database check constraint refuses it.

Given mvp_compliance/exceptions.py, when PublishError and PublishedVersionError are inspected, then each has a docstring naming the requirement it holds, and neither is a subclass of django.core.exceptions.ValidationError.

Given a draft, when publish() is called, then the whole act happens inside one transaction: the document's row is locked with select_for_update(), the previously current version becomes superseded, and this version becomes current with its publication time set.

Given a document with a version in force, when a second row is forced to the current status behind publish()'s back, then the database raises IntegrityError — the one-current-version-per-document rule is enforced by a constraint, not only by the method.

Given a document with two drafts, when both are published one after the other, then the document still reports exactly one version in force, and the test proves it without wall-clock timing or thread scheduling.
Given the Version model and its queryset, when they are inspected by name, then none of unpublish, revert, rollback, restore or make_current exists on either.
Given the model changes in this story, when makemigrations has run, then makemigrations --check is clean and migrate from an empty database reaches the same schema.
